To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bonding process of microstructured shallow microfluidic chips made from COP Zeonex® 690R is optimized by the use of plasma-assisted solvent bonding at 120 °C, 2 MPa, 10 s.
the bonding process of shallow microfluidics can be optimized by the use of solvent-assisted plasma bonding, a temperature range of 150–170 °C, and a pressure range of 1–3 bar.
the bonding of shallow microfluidics made from COP is possible and can be optimized by a systematic and practical approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a practical approach to the optimization of channel deformation in the sealing of microfluidic devices.

the development of a practical and systematic approach to the optimization of channel deformation during the fabrication of microfluidic devices, which will be beneficial for the design and fabrication of shallow microfluidics.
the optimization of the channel integrity of shallow microfluidics devices made from COP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
solvent-assisted bonding of COP Zeonex at 150 °C for 1 h is a suitable method for the sealing of shallow COP devices, while plasma-assisted bonding is not recommended for this purpose.
solvent-assisted bonding is the most suitable bonding technique for the sealing of shallow COP microfluidic devices.

the use of Zeonex 390R (Tg > 200 °C) as the substrate material, and the use of Zeoform ZF14 (native Tg = 135 °C) for sealing, is the preferred combination for the manufacture of shallow microfluidics devices made from Zeonex 680R.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimization of channel deformation in shallow microfluidic COP devices is possible.
the presented approach enables a systematic and reliable optimization of the sealing process of shallow microfluidics devices.
the presented approach is suitable for the optimization of bonding parameters for the sealing of shallow devices made of COP, and it is also applicable for the sealing of other thermoplastics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a systematic approach can help identify a suitable bonding process for shallow microfluidic channels made from COP, which is a polymer that is increasingly used in microfluidic applications.
a simple mechanical analysis can be used as a basis for the optimization of the sealing parameters for the fabrication of shallow microfluidics made from COP.
a systematic approach for the optimization and characterization of bonding parameters can be successfully applied to the sealing of shallow LOC devices made from COP materials.
